:topic/_next.:topic/title: Distributing the Negative Sign in a Linear Expression

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Performing the operations on each corresponding entry, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(B-C) & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 2 & -2\end{bmatrix}-(\begin{bmatrix}-1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}0 & -5 \\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}) \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 2 & -2\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}-1-0 & -1-(-5) \\ 2-1 & 0-1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 2 & -2\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-1-(-1) & 0-4 \\ 2-1 & -2-(-1)\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Calculating the Sum or Difference of Three or More Matrices

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we simplify the expression by distributing the subtraction over the matrices in the parentheses: 

$$
\begin{aligned}A+C-(B+A) & =A+C-B-A \\  & =\cancel{A}+C-B-\cancel{A} \\  & =C-B\end{aligned}
$$

We are left with a single subtraction. So, we subtract the corresponding entries of the two matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}C-B & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ -6 & 1\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}3-3 & -1-(-1) \\ 1-2 & 2-0 \\ -6-(-4) & 1-1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
